about: Task 8 of the BBC Micro models plan: the points marked by hand for the outside model, in their own file because marks.json is pinned by hash to task 5's run. Each is read by eye off a crop of the original input: the box (left, top, right, bottom, in the original's pixels) enlarged zoom times with a grid labelled in the original's pixels. Pixel coordinates are the original's, with (0, 0) the top left corner of the top left pixel's centre.
what: Task 8's points, for the outside model, read by eye off crops of the originals (the crop's box and zoom beside each; the grid every 10 px unless `grid` says 5 or 20), in the original's pixels. A corner of the case or of the keyboard's opening is where the flat beige top ends: where the line of one edge meets the line of the other, outside any strip of the opening's inner wall that a view shows. An LED's point is the middle of its dark disc, not its highlight. `seeds` are rough key centres (to about 10 px), read on gridded overviews, only to start the search for each legend in keys.py; nothing is measured from them.

checkKey.why: The side profile's check point (the plan's row: within 2.0 mm of where it is measured), chosen before any camera was fitted: the key A's legend, found in O4 and O5 as every other key's is, is left out of the camera fit, triangulated with the two cameras, and compared with where K1 puts it, on the key plane. A is the leftmost letter of its row, near the side the profile is of.

caseTop.what: The case top's four corners, for its registration to the Service Manual's 415 by 345 mm. The front two are task 0's marks (keys.frontEdge), not read again; the rear two are read here.

opening.what: The keyboard's opening in the case top: its four corners where the flat top ends. The rear two lie against the badge strip.

badge.what: The badge strip across the back of the opening: its front edge at each end (its back is the opening's rear edge), and the box of its two lines of words. The owl, right of the words from x 1948 to 2015, is not drawn and not measured.

leds.what: The three lights, left to right, each under its printed words: cassette motor, caps lock, shift lock.

seeds.what: Rough key centres for the legend search (keys.py), each read on a gridded overview of the whole photograph; about 10 px.

o4o5.what: Points marked in both O4 and O5, for the two cameras and to be triangulated. O4 and O5 have had their backgrounds painted white, and the paint cuts across some of the case's corners and edges, so no point on the case's outline is used: only points inside it.

o2.what: The rear, nearly square on. Its background is painted white too, so the case's ends are the paint's edge; they are used only to put the board in the case, not in the rear ports' check. The DIN sockets show only the lit lower arc of their rims, so each is a few points along its arc, and its centre is the circle through them (case_parts.py). The others are centres read directly.

dsubPosts.what: the middles of the 15-way D's two hexagonal posts, which stand in its mounting holes

caseEnds.what: the case's two ends at y 580, just under the seam, where the rear face's ends stand upright; the machine's right is the photograph's left

rearFace.what: the rear face's top edge (where the top's light ends) and its bottom edge, at x 1000

ports.label: UHF out
ports.what: the middle of its ring's left, right, top and bottom edges

ports.label: video out
ports.what: the middle of its ring's edges; it stands out of the panel

ports.label: analogue in
ports.what: the middle of the two posts

vents.what: the two slots across the top of the black panel: each one's ends in x, and their top and bottom in y

mains.what: the mains panel at the machine's left rear: its black plate's box, and its words as far as they can be read

o8.what: The underside, read by eye on the whole 640 by 311 picture: the words printed beside the five connectors under the front, left to right as the picture shows them (seen from below, so the machine's right is the picture's left), and the socket beside them.
